title: Krishna Passes Away
body:
Krishna Passes Away

The wheel of time moved relentlessly toward the dawn of the Kali Yuga. In Dwaraka, the Yadavas, intoxicated by power, prosperity, and Sree Krishna's protective presence, had degenerated into arrogance and vanity. The cosmic curse of the sages—triggered when some mischievous Yadava youths dressed Prince Samba as a woman and mockingly asked the sages to predict her child's sex—began to take effect. Samba gave birth to an iron mace. Though the terrified Yadavas ground the mace into fine powder and scattered it in the ocean, fate could not be bypassed. The powder washed ashore and grew into a dense crop of sharp rushes (Erakas). Years later, during a drunken festival by the sea, a minor argument erupted among the Yadavas. Grabbing the rushes, which transformed back into iron maces, they attacked and slaughtered one another, bringing about the complete annihilation of the Yadava clan.
Seeing the destruction of His lineage and realising that His mission on earth was completed, Sree Krishna retired to the quiet forest. Reclining under a tree, He withdrew His consciousness into the inner self. A hunter named Jara, mistaking the Lord's reddish lotus-foot for the eye of a deer, shot a sharp arrow from a distance. The arrow pierced His foot. Approaching, Jara saw the Divine Personality and wept in absolute terror. Krishna blessed him and, through His supreme, free will, cast off His mortal frame and returned to His eternal, blemishless abode (Paramapadam), signalling the dark dawn of the Kali Yuga.
